newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end stronger, pulled up by U.S. gains.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end stronger, pulled up by U.S. gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Thursday, pulled higher by sharp gains in U.S. Treasuries, with Canadian economic data having little impact on prices, analysts said.

"What you tend to get on a day like this are general flows into the North American basket. Canada picks up off that and benefits from some of those flows," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed-income research with ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$2.00 to C$110.55 to yield 7.109 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond rose 1-16/32 to yield 6.59 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 52 basis points from 57 basis points at Wednesday's close.

Canadian bonds opened firmer with U.S. Treasuries this morning, following reports showing a narrower-than-expected U.S. trade deficit and higher-than-expected U.S. jobless claims data. Canadian and U.S. bonds firmed further this afternoon amid strong demand at an auction of US$12.5 billion in five year notes.
"Obviously we're just tracking the U.S.," said one dealer. "Maybe a few people were short and panicking and paying a little bit more."

Stronger-than-expected Canadian economic data out this morning had little impact on bond prices, analysts said. Canadian retail sales rose 1.1 percent in October, Statistics Canada reported. Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast a 0.5 percent rise. Another report showed Canada's merchandise trade fell more than expected.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$1.38 to C$103.85 to 6.468 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 30/32 to yield 6.33 percent.
The spread between the bonds narrowed to 14 basis points from 19 basis points at Wednesday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.90 percent against the U.S. bill at 4.99 percent.
